entries.exactTarget: Determine whether the six-dimensional sphere S^6 admits an integrable complex structure.
entries.qualification: Resolved affirmatively: the six-sphere admits an integrable complex structure. Philip Engel provides a self-contained proof and states that he independently verified its mathematical content. Google DeepMind’s Formal Conjectures project also classifies the problem as solved and links a Lean formalization. The earlier Open label came from older evidence. This status review did not include a local Lean replay or establish journal acceptance.

Google DeepMind Formal Conjectures, MathOverflow 1973: solved status and linked Lean formalization, pinned revision 6fbb54f24ccc2e64dcfaffc28c58950e377110d2.

entries.exactTarget: Prove that there is a universal constant c > 0 such that for every collection of vectors v_1, ..., v_n in the Euclidean unit ball B_2^d (any d, n), there exist signs epsilon_1, ..., epsilon_n in {-1,1} with || sum_i epsilon_i v_i ||_infinity <= c.
entries.qualification: User reports the linked proof passes audit. The coordinator verifies the exact theorem and the incidence-matrix implication, without claiming a new independent proof audit, peer review or formal verification. Exact match: the listing requires some universal constant c for all d,n and arbitrary real vectors in the Euclidean unit ball. Theorem 1.2 supplies c=36 with precisely the same sign and infinity-norm conditions. The argument on PDF page 3 passes from rational to real inputs, so there is no rational-only limitation. No optimal constant or efficient algorithm is required by our listing.

sources.citation: An elementary proof of the Komlós conjecture, Theorem 1.2, PDF page 2; real-vector passage on PDF page 3

entries.exactTarget: Prove that there is a universal constant C such that every hypergraph H in which each vertex lies in at most t edges has discrepancy at most C sqrt(t).
entries.qualification: User reports the linked proof passes audit. The coordinator verifies the exact theorem and the incidence-matrix implication, without claiming a new independent proof audit, peer review or formal verification. Exact implication: for a finite hypergraph of maximum vertex degree t>0, use one row per edge and one column a_v per vertex in its 0/1 incidence matrix. Each column has Euclidean norm at most sqrt(t). Apply Theorem 1.2 to a_v/sqrt(t). Multiplying back gives a vertex signing with absolute signed sum at most 36 sqrt(t) in every edge. For t=0 all edge sums are zero. This proves the listed universal C sqrt(t) target with C=36, not merely the older linear-in-t bound.

entries.exactTarget: Determine the zero-error capacity C_0(p) of the binary symmetric channel with error probability p under complete noiseless feedback.
entries.qualification: For the ordinary memoryless BSC, fixed-blocklength zero-error capacity with noiseless feedback is zero for 0<p<1 and one bit per use at deterministic endpoints p=0 or p=1. Under either message and any causal feedback encoding strategy every finite output word has positive probability when 0<p<1. Thus two messages cannot have disjoint decoding supports. A single message gives zero rate; deterministic endpoints transmit one bit exactly. An adversarial bounded-error-fraction or list-decoding problem is a distinct target. The Berlekamp citation does not change the written random-error-probability formulation. No retitling, rank transfer or substitute target is authorized.

records.canonicalTitle: P versus NP
records.exactTarget: Determine whether P = NP, that is, whether every decision problem whose solutions can be verified in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine can also be solved in polynomial time by a deterministic Turing machine.

records.readerQualification: P versus NP remains open on the maintained Clay statement and the bounded claim sweep; no accepted exact-target resolution was established.
records.readerQuestion: When a yes-or-no problem has short evidence for each yes answer that can be checked in polynomial time, must a deterministic computer also be able to solve the problem in polynomial time? Here polynomial time measures how the work grows with the input size.
records.familyLabel: Classical complexity separations
records.whyItMatters: Equality would give polynomial-time algorithms for every NP decision problem; separation would establish that some efficiently checkable problems resist all such algorithms. This addresses computational efficiency as input size grows.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: An equality proof would give deterministic polynomial-time algorithms for every NP decision problem.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A separation would establish an NP language with no deterministic polynomial-time decision algorithm.

records.canonicalTitle: Riemann Hypothesis
records.exactTarget: For the meromorphic continuation of the Riemann zeta function zeta(s)=sum_{n>=1} n^(-s), initially defined for Re(s)>1, every zero s in the open critical strip 0<Re(s)<1 has Re(s)=1/2. This is the Riemann Hypothesis for zeta alone; it does not assert simplicity of its zeros.
records.statusQualification: Riemann remains open. September 2026 progress on the proportion of simple critical-line zeros is partial, not proof that every nontrivial zero lies on the line. Uncorroborated or inaccessible proof claims were not accepted.
records.readerQualification: Riemann remains open. September 2026 progress on the proportion of simple critical-line zeros is partial, not proof that every nontrivial zero lies on the line. Uncorroborated or inaccessible proof claims were not accepted.
records.readerQuestion: Do all zeros of the Riemann zeta function inside the strip with real part between zero and one lie exactly on its middle line?
records.familyLabel: Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros
records.whyItMatters: A proof would sharply control fluctuations in the distribution of primes: the prime-counting function would differ from its logarithmic-integral approximation by at most O(√x log x). A disproof would invalidate this equivalent error bound.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof establishes the equivalent pi(x)=Li(x)+O(sqrt(x)log(x)) bound described by Bombieri, sharply controlling prime-counting fluctuations. Applications requiring additional L-function hypotheses are not automatically obtained.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof makes that equivalent prime-counting error bound false and supplies an obstruction to the proposed zeta-zero pattern. Other conditional implications remain valid as implications; their conclusions do not automatically all fail.

records.canonicalTitle: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
records.exactTarget: For every compact simple gauge group G, prove that a nontrivial four-dimensional quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 exists with all existence requirements of Jaffe-Witten, Quantum Yang-Mills Theory, sections 3-4, including axiomatic properties at least as strong as their cited references [45,35], the required gauge-invariant local fields and short-distance compatibility specified there. The official reconstruction and existence requirements are retained by reference, not replaced by an unrestricted equivalence of arbitrary Euclidean and Minkowski theories. An isolated first excited eigenstate, confinement and asymptotic completeness are not additional requirements.

records.readerQuestion: Can a nontrivial Yang–Mills quantum field theory in four-dimensional spacetime be constructed rigorously for every compact simple gauge group—the choice of internal symmetry—with a positive, finite gap between vacuum energy and the remaining energy spectrum?
records.familyLabel: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap

resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution identifies a permitted group for which the official conjunction cannot hold, forcing revision of that universal mathematical target without by itself invalidating experimental observations or every other quantum field theory.

records.canonicalTitle: Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness: Fefferman A
records.exactTarget: Prove Fefferman statement (A): for every viscosity nu > 0 and every real smooth divergence-free Schwartz vector field u0 on R^3, with force f identically zero, there are real velocity u and pressure p in C-infinity(R^3 x [0,infinity)) satisfying partial_t u + (u dot grad)u = nu Delta u - grad p, div u = 0 and u(x,0) = u0(x). The velocity energy integral over R^3 of |u(x,t)|^2 is bounded above by one finite constant for all t >= 0; that constant may depend on u0 and nu. Schwartz means every spatial derivative decays faster than every inverse polynomial, as in official condition (4). Smoothness includes time zero. The selected domain is whole space, not the torus.
records.statusQualification: The ranked target is Fefferman A: unforced whole-space Navier–Stokes regularity for smooth rapidly decaying divergence-free data. OpenAI's September claim addresses forced alternatives C/D, not A. Retain open for this exact target; no proof acceptance is inferred from the broader prize announcement.

records.readerQuestion: For an incompressible fluid filling three-dimensional space, with any positive viscosity and no external force, does every smooth, rapidly decaying initial velocity give a flow that stays smooth forever, with uniformly bounded total kinetic energy?

records.readerQuestion: Do one-way functions exist: functions that a deterministic computer can evaluate in polynomial time, but that every randomized polynomial-time algorithm reverses on a random input’s output with success eventually smaller than every inverse power of the input length? Reversing means finding any input with that output.
records.familyLabel: One-way functions and permutations
records.whyItMatters: A construction would unconditionally separate efficient forward computation from hard inversion on random inputs, even when the inverter uses randomness. Every randomized polynomial-time inverter would have only negligible success probability as input length grows.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: An unconditional construction with a proof of negligible PPT inversion probability would establish existence under the standard definition and instantiate consequences already proved from OWFs.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: An impossibility theorem for every polynomial-time function family under the standard inversion experiment would rule out classical one-way functions and assumptions equivalent to their existence.

records.canonicalTitle: Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions
records.exactTarget: For every integer q>=1 and every Dirichlet character chi modulo q, including principal and imprimitive characters, every zero s of the meromorphic continuation of L(s,chi)=sum_{n>=1}chi(n)n^(-s) in 0<Re(s)<1 satisfies Re(s)=1/2. The continuation is from Re(s)>1. Only open-strip zeros are quantified: principal-character poles and boundary zeros of imprimitive Euler factors are not counterexamples. No simplicity or central nonvanishing requirement is added.
records.statusQualification: Dirichlet GRH remains open. No independently established full-target resolution was obtained; neighboring Riemann-family claims and source-access limitations remain qualified.
records.readerQualification: Dirichlet GRH remains open. No independently established full-target resolution was obtained; neighboring Riemann-family claims and source-access limitations remain qualified.
records.readerQuestion: Dirichlet L-functions extend the zeta-function setting by using periodic arithmetic weights. For every Dirichlet character, do all zeros of its L-function with real part between zero and one lie on the middle line, with real part one-half?
records.familyLabel: Riemann hypotheses and exceptional zeros
records.whyItMatters: A proof would bound how far one must search for a prime in an arithmetic progression. For q > 3 and a coprime to q, the least prime congruent to a modulo q would be at most (φ(q) log q)², where φ(q) counts the residue classes coprime to q.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof makes LLS's GRH-conditional least-prime estimate unconditional: for q>3 and gcd(a,q)=1, the least prime congruent to a modulo q is at most (phi(q)log(q))^2.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof establishes an off-line Dirichlet zero and invalidates the general hypothesis. Theorems conditional on GRH remain true implications; particular prime-distribution or algorithmic conclusions are not thereby automatically false.

records.canonicalTitle: NP versus P/poly
records.exactTarget: Determine the truth of NP subseteq P/poly. Here NP consists of languages over finite binary strings accepted by nondeterministic Turing machines in polynomial time. P/poly consists of languages L for which there exist constants C>=1 and integer k>=1 and Boolean circuits C_n for all n>=0, of size at most C(n+1)^k, deciding membership in L on every length-n input. Circuits are finite acyclic single-output circuits with fan-in-two AND/OR, fan-in-one NOT, input bits and hardwired constants0/1; count all nodes. Each language has its own bound and circuit family, with no uniform generation requirement.
records.statusQualification: NP containment in nonuniform P/poly remains open; February 2026 notes pose the matching general-circuit question. Restricted circuits and Karp–Lipton implications do not decide it.
records.readerQualification: NP containment in nonuniform P/poly remains open; February 2026 notes pose the matching general-circuit question. Restricted circuits and Karp–Lipton implications do not decide it.
records.readerQuestion: Can every yes-or-no problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers be solved by Boolean circuits of polynomial size, if a separate circuit may be chosen for each input length? No efficient method of constructing those circuits is required.
records.familyLabel: NP versus P/poly
records.whyItMatters: Containment would collapse the polynomial hierarchy to its second level by the Karp–Lipton theorem. Noncontainment would establish a general circuit-size barrier for an NP language and imply P ≠ NP.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: By the Karp–Lipton theorem, NP containment in P/poly collapses the polynomial hierarchy to its second level. The circuits' nonuniform existence alone does not give a deterministic polynomial-time SAT algorithm.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Noncontainment gives a superpolynomial general Boolean-circuit obstruction for an NP language and implies P!=NP because P is contained in P/poly. It does not by itself establish average-case hardness or secure cryptography.

records.canonicalTitle: BQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation
records.exactTarget: Determine the truth values of BOTH NP subseteq BQP and BQP subseteq NP for unrelativized, advice-free classes of total languages over {0,1}. NP consists of languages with polynomial-length binary witnesses and a deterministic polynomial-time verifier. BQP consists of languages decided by polynomial-time uniformly generated polynomial-size quantum circuits (a deterministic Turing machine outputs Q_n on 1^n), using Watrous's fixed Toffoli, Hadamard and phase-i gates with |0> ancillas and discarding, followed by a standard-basis output measurement. On every yes input acceptance is at least 2/3, and on every no input it is at most 1/3. No arbitrary real gate constants, advice or oracle are available. Establish equality, either proper containment, or incomparability.
records.statusQualification: Both unrelativized BQP/NP inclusions remain unresolved on the checked evidence. Random-permutation oracle separations do not settle the frozen uniform total-language relationship.
records.readerQualification: Both unrelativized BQP/NP inclusions remain unresolved on the checked evidence. Random-permutation oracle separations do not settle the stated uniform total-language relationship.
records.readerQuestion: How do efficient quantum solving and efficient classical verification compare for yes-or-no problems? Does quantum computation with bounded error solve every problem with short, efficiently checkable evidence for yes answers—and do all problems it solves have such evidence?
records.familyLabel: BQP Versus NP: Complete Language-Class Relation
records.whyItMatters: Resolving both inclusions would determine whether these computational classes coincide, one strictly contains the other, or neither contains the other. Each outcome gives a different relationship between efficient verification and bounded-error quantum computation.

resolutionConsequences.completeResolution: A full determination fixes whether efficient quantum computation encompasses all NP languages and whether every BQP language admits efficient classical witness verification. Equality, either proper containment and incomparability are all valid complete answers; consequences must follow the relation actually proved.

records.exactTarget: There exists a total algorithm which, given any finite encoding of a multivariate polynomial f in Z[x_1,...,x_n] with arbitrary finite n and integer coefficients, halts and correctly decides whether there is q in Q^n with f(q)=0. records.canonicalTitle: Matrix-Multiplication Exponent Equals Two
records.exactTarget: Let R_Q(n) be the tensor rank over Q of the bilinear map multiplying two n by n rational matrices: the least r for which AB is a sum of r products alpha_j(A) beta_j(B) C_j, with rational linear forms alpha_j, beta_j and rational output matrices C_j. Set omega_Q = inf{tau in R : R_Q(n) = O(n^tau)}. Prove omega_Q = 2. Equivalently, for every epsilon > 0, exact multiplication admits division-free arithmetic circuits over Q of size O(n^(2+epsilon)), counting rational additions, subtractions, multiplications and constant scalar operations at unit cost. Circuits need not be uniformly generated and rational coefficient bit lengths are not charged. Constants and thresholds may depend on epsilon. Literal O(n^2) attainment is not required.

records.canonicalTitle: Unique Games Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every fixed pair of real constants epsilon, delta > 0 with epsilon + delta < 1, there exists an integer k >= 2, depending only on epsilon and delta, such that the following promise problem is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time many-one reductions. An instance is a finite directed constraint graph G=(V,E) with E nonempty and, for each edge e=(v,w), a permutation pi_e of [k]. For a labeling L:V->[k], an edge is satisfied if pi_e(L(v))=L(w); val(G) is the largest fraction of satisfied edges over all labelings. Distinguish val(G) >= 1-epsilon from val(G) <= delta, with no requirement on instances between these thresholds. The graph is the growing input; epsilon, delta and k are fixed constants. NP-hardness means that every language in NP has such a reduction mapping yes inputs to the first promised set and no inputs to the second.
records.statusQualification: Classical UGC remains open. Root checked that the accessible Hallelujah preprint's graphwise ratio strictly below 2 does not give the fixed uniform 2-epsilon improvement needed for its claimed contradiction. The linked journal full text was inaccessible; no independent acceptance of a full disproof was established.
records.readerQualification: Classical UGC remains open. The accessible Hallelujah preprint's graphwise ratio strictly below 2 does not give the fixed uniform 2-epsilon improvement needed for its claimed contradiction. The linked journal full text was inaccessible; independent acceptance of a full disproof was not established.
records.readerQuestion: In a graph-labeling game, each edge requires the two labels to match through a one-to-one rule. Is distinguishing games where almost all rules can be satisfied from those where only a tiny fraction can be satisfied NP-hard, however small these two error thresholds are, with a fixed label set chosen for each pair of thresholds?
records.familyLabel: Unique Games Conjecture
records.whyItMatters: A proof would establish this hardness gap and support approximation thresholds obtained through Unique Games reductions. Claims of efficient-algorithm impossibility from NP-hardness would still require the assumption P ≠ NP.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof supplies the universal constant-gap NP-hardness premise used in existing gap-preserving reductions and associated approximation-threshold results. resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A refutation identifies a failure of the universal hardness premise. It would require reassessing conclusions whose only available hardness justification assumes that premise, but does not negate the proved conditional implications, disprove every individual hardness result or automatically provide approximation algorithms.

records.exactTarget: For every field k, every Weil cohomology theory H* available over k, every smooth projective k-variety X of pure dimension n, every integer r with 0<=r<=n, and every rational algebraic cycle z of codimension r on X, if deg(z.w)=0 for every rational algebraic cycle w of codimension n-r on X, then the H* cycle class of z is zero. Equivalently, numerical and H*-homological equivalence of rational algebraic cycles agree in every codimension.
records.statusQualification: Standard Conjecture D remains open_with_solved_subcases. The August 2026 abelian-fourfold claim does not cover all smooth projective varieties; earlier conditional uses neither prove the universal target nor corroborate the newest claim.
records.readerQualification: Standard Conjecture D remains open, with solved subcases. The August 2026 abelian-fourfold claim does not cover all smooth projective varieties; earlier conditional uses neither prove the universal target nor corroborate the newest claim.
records.readerQuestion: On a smooth projective variety, do rational algebraic cycles that give the same intersection numbers against every complementary cycle necessarily have the same class in every available Weil cohomology theory?
records.familyLabel: Grothendieck’s standard conjectures
records.whyItMatters: A proof would make intersection numbers sufficient to detect homological vanishing in every codimension and cohomology theory in scope. A counterexample would separate numerical equivalence from homological equivalence.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof identifies numerical equivalence with homological equivalence throughout the specified Weil-cohomological settings, making numerical cycle information sufficient to determine homological vanishing. Numerical-motive semisimplicity is already unconditional and is not a new reward.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof exhibits a genuine gap between intersection-theoretic numerical vanishing and cohomological vanishing. It invalidates universal identifications relying on D, not every separate standard conjecture without a checked implication.

records.canonicalTitle: The Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture on Geometric Galois Representations
records.exactTarget: Let K be a number field and l a prime. Every irreducible continuous finite-dimensional l-adic representation rho of Gal(Kbar/K), unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at every place above l, occurs as a subquotient of H^i_et(X_Kbar)(m) for some smooth projective variety X over K, integer i >= 0, and integer Tate twist m. Etale cohomology is taken with the same l-adic coefficient field as rho. There is no nonnegative Hodge-Tate weight restriction.
records.statusQualification: The full corrected assertion is open_with_solved_subcases as a scope-based current-status inference, not proof certification. Newton describes dimension-one cases and Thorne August2026 states a narrower still-conjectural GL2 case with restricted new results. No claim of universal present-status quotation is made.
records.readerQualification: The full conjecture remains open, with solved subcases. The one-dimensional case is known; Thorne’s August 2026 preprint treats restricted two-dimensional cases and does not establish the assertion for every number field and dimension. This status is inferred from the reviewed scopes, not a certification of the proofs.
records.readerQuestion: A Galois representation records arithmetic symmetries as matrices. Must every irreducible l-adic representation over a number field, unramified outside finitely many places and de Rham at primes above l—a local condition describing behavior expected from geometry—come from a smooth projective variety’s cohomology, allowing subquotients and Tate twists?
records.familyLabel: The Fontaine-Mazur Conjecture on Geometric Galois Representations
records.whyItMatters: A proof would make these arithmetic conditions sufficient for geometric realization across all number fields and finite dimensions. The realization may use any integer Tate twist, including negative twists, and imposes no nonnegative Hodge–Tate weight restriction.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: The arithmetic hypotheses would suffice for twisted geometric realization throughout the frozen scope. This is the direct meaning of the assertion in Hajir and Shin–Templier, not an algorithm for finding a variety. Newton's additional automorphy and L-function consequences explicitly require Langlands reciprocity.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A qualifying representation with no such realization would refute sufficiency of the stated hypotheses, while preserving already proved cases. This is the logical complement of the sourced geometric-realization assertion; it would not by itself refute theorems about cohomology or prove a failure of Langlands reciprocity.

records.canonicalTitle: BQP versus QMA
records.exactTarget: For promise problems A=(A_yes,A_no) with disjoint sets of finite binary strings, use polynomial-time uniform quantum circuits over a fixed effectively specified finite universal gate set, with polynomially many gates and |0> ancillas and a measured output bit. BQP has such a circuit accepting each yes input with probability>=2/3 and each no input with probability<=1/3. QMA permits a polynomial-length quantum witness: each yes input has a witness accepted with probability>=2/3, and every witness on each no input is accepted with probability<=1/3. Outside the promise no condition is imposed. Is QMA contained in BQP, equivalently BQP=QMA?
records.statusQualification: BQP versus QMA remains open for unrelativized uniform promise classes. Unitary/classical oracle results and August qIO work with an assumed average-case QMA gap do not decide that equality.
records.readerQualification: BQP versus QMA remains open for unrelativized uniform promise classes. Unitary/classical oracle results and August qIO work with an assumed average-case QMA gap do not decide that equality.
records.readerQuestion: If a quantum computer can efficiently check a supplied quantum proof for a promised yes-or-no problem, can it also solve that problem efficiently without receiving the proof? Both verification and solving allow bounded error.
records.familyLabel: BQP versus QMA
records.whyItMatters: Equality would give efficient quantum decision procedures for QMA-complete promise problems, including the standard local-Hamiltonian energy-threshold problem. Separation would show that quantum witnesses add decision power beyond efficient quantum computation alone.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Equality would yield efficient bounded-error quantum decision procedures for QMA-complete promise problems, including the standard two-local Hamiltonian energy-threshold problem. It would not automatically prepare witnesses or ground states or break every quantum cryptographic primitive.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Separation would prove that quantum verification with polynomial quantum proofs is strictly stronger than witness-free efficient quantum decision computation. QMA-completeness would then rule out BQP decision algorithms for the standard complete promise problems.

records.canonicalTitle: Existence of One-Way Permutations
records.exactTarget: There exists a family f_n:{0,1}^n->{0,1}^n, n>=1, of bijections computed by one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm on (1^n,x), such that for every probabilistic polynomial-time algorithm A its inversion success Pr[A(1^n,f_n(x))=x], over uniform x and A's coins, is negligible in n: for every c>0 it is at most n^(-c) for all sufficiently large n. This is unconditional existence in the classical unrelativized model, with no key sampling or variable domains.
records.statusQualification: Unconditional one-way permutations remain open. Full-domain trapdoor constructions require iO and one-way functions; query inversion taking square-root domain size is exponential in bit length and does not refute classical polynomial-time security.
records.readerQualification: Unconditional one-way permutations remain open. Full-domain trapdoor constructions require iO and one-way functions; query inversion taking square-root domain size is exponential in bit length and does not refute classical polynomial-time security.
records.readerQuestion: Can one polynomial-time algorithm permute binary strings bijectively at every length n, while every randomized polynomial-time algorithm reverses a random output with success smaller than every inverse power of n for sufficiently large n?
records.familyLabel: One-way functions and permutations
records.whyItMatters: A proof would establish computationally hard inversion even when every output has exactly one preimage and the domain is all n-bit strings. The guarantee would hold uniformly across lengths in the classical model without oracles or sampled keys.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Prove existence of an in-scope uniform polynomial-time full-domain length-preserving permutation family whose inversion success is negligible for EVERY PPT adversary.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Prove that EVERY in-scope uniform polynomial-time full-domain permutation family has SOME PPT inverter with non-negligible success: some c>0 has success greater than n^(-c) for infinitely many n. Breaking one candidate or proving a restricted black-box barrier is insufficient.

records.canonicalTitle: Equivariant Tamagawa number conjecture: Burns-Flach Conjecture4 package
records.exactTarget: For every motive M over a number field K in Burns-Flach Section3.1's motivic-structure formalism, with an action of a finite-dimensional semisimple Q-algebra A, and every order mathcal A in A admitting the compatible projective mathcal A-structure of Section3.3, prove Burns-Flach Conjecture4(i)-(iv) in its stated conditional setting. The external defining hypotheses are the finite motivic cohomology and real comparison exact sequence of Conjecture1, the motivic-to-p-adic comparison of Conjecture2 for M and Mdual(1), coefficient compatibility giving well-defined equivariant local factors as in4.1 (Conjecture3 or the weaker Euler-factor compatibility of Remark7), and the stated Coherence hypothesis. A projective structure consists of full projective lattices in the archimedean realizations whose l-adic comparison images agree and are Galois-stable, not merely an arbitrary maximal-order choice. The INCLUDED assertions are: (i) the finite equivariant L-function L(AM,s) has meromorphic continuation to0; (ii) its componentwise integer order r equals rr_A(H_f^1(K,Mdual(1))^*)-rr_A(H_f^0(K,Mdual(1))^*), with reduced rank as in2.6; (iii) for the nonzero componentwise leading Laurent coefficient L*(AM,0)=lim_(s->0) s^(-r)L(AM,s), the class T_Omega=delta_hat^1_(mathcal A,R)(L*(AM,0))+R_Omega(M,mathcal A) lies in Cl(mathcal A,Q); and (iv) T_Omega=0 in Cl(mathcal A,R), hence in K_0(mathcal A,R). The R_Omega term is the class of the fundamental virtual object with its integral compact-support cohomology structures and real comparison trivialization in3.4; delta_hat is Lemma9's canonical extended reduced-norm boundary, not an inverse to a surjective real reduced norm. Equivalently the final identity is delta_hat(L*)=-R_Omega. Preserve graded determinant conventions and all suitable nonmaximal/noncommutative orders. Coherence-free Remark8's Conjecture5 and Conjecture6 for EVERY prime are an alternative to the rational/integral clauses in the source's stated sense, not removal of(i)-(ii) or replacement by a single p-local or epsilon assertion. The external hypotheses are not presumed universally proved or restricted to currently established cases, and proving all of them is not added as a separate conclusion.

records.canonicalTitle: Deligne conjecture on coefficient-equivariant critical motivic L-values
records.exactTarget: For every pure motive M over Q with coefficients in a number field E, in Deligne's geometric realization formalism (Betti, de Rham and compatible l-adic realizations with comparison, dual, tensor and Tate-twist structures), and every critical integer n, the normalized finite L-value vector L(M,n)/((2*pi*i)^(n*d_sign)*c^sign(M)) lies in the diagonal E inside E tensor C, where sign=(-1)^n and d_sign=dim_E H_B^sign(M). Here H_B^sign is the sign eigenspace of complex conjugation, and c^sign is the determinant of the Betti/de Rham comparison to the corresponding filtration quotient, computed in E-rational bases and defined modulo E-units as in Deligne1.7/2.6. Critical means that L_infinity(sigma,M,s) and L_infinity(sigma,Mdual,1-s) have no pole at s=n for every embedding sigma:E->C (equivalently use Mdual(1) at -s). Use finite, not completed, L-functions with the compatible E-valued local factors of2.2. Analytic continuation giving finite values at the selected critical integer and the source's well-defined compatible realizations/local factors are defining prerequisites, not assertions proved by this period law and not a restriction to cases whose continuation is already known. The simultaneous embedding vector must come from one element of E; unrelated componentwise algebraicity is insufficient. All-zero values are allowed, but mixed zero/nonzero components do not satisfy the diagonal membership. No general nonvanishing or order-of-zero assertion from Deligne2.7 is appended.

records.canonicalTitle: FPT versus W[1]
records.exactTarget: Prove or disprove FPT!=W[1] in classical uniform parameterized complexity. Equivalently, determine whether there is a deterministic algorithm, a total computable function f:N->N and an absolute constant c such that on every finite simple n-vertex graph G and every integer 1<=k<=n it decides the existence of a k-clique within f(k)n^c steps. The conjecture asserts no such algorithm. The function and exponent are fixed with the algorithm; no input-length advice, oracle or nonuniform circuit family is allowed.
records.statusQualification: FPT versus W[1] remains open. Yi's counting-collapse claim was explicitly withdrawn May 10, 2026; independent 2026 work retains the separation as an assumption. The ordinary uniform k-Clique target is unchanged.
records.readerQualification: FPT versus W[1] remains open. Yi's counting-collapse claim was explicitly withdrawn May 10, 2026; independent 2026 work retains the separation as an assumption. The ordinary uniform k-Clique target is unchanged.
records.readerQuestion: Can we deterministically decide whether an n-vertex graph contains k mutually connected vertices in time f(k)n^c, for some computable function f and fixed constant c independent of k? This would confine any non-polynomial growth in the bound to the chosen clique size k.
records.familyLabel: FPT versus W[1]
records.whyItMatters: Such an algorithm would confine the parameter-dependent cost to f(k) while keeping the input-size exponent fixed. Proving none exists would separate FPT from W[1] in the stated uniform model.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A separation establishes that the complete parameterized Clique problem has no allowed FPT decider and supports the usual intractability conclusions obtained via W[1]-hardness reductions.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: An FPT Clique algorithm transfers through W[1]-completeness reductions to all W[1] problems. Its parameter dependence may grow arbitrarily fast computably, so equality alone does not give a polynomial-time Clique algorithm in the full input size.

records.canonicalTitle: Weight–Monodromy Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let K be ANY nonarchimedean local field with finite residue field F_q of characteristic p, X ANY proper smooth variety over K, i>=0, and l ANY prime different from p. Put V=H^i_et(X_over_Kbar,Qbar_l), retaining the original K. On an open inertia subgroup the action is unipotent and defines nilpotent monodromy N:V->V(-1), with its Galois-equivariant Tate twist. Let M be the unique increasing monodromy filtration centred at zero: N(M_j) is contained in M_(j-2)(-1), and N^a:gr^M_a(V)->gr^M_(-a)(V)(-a) is an isomorphism for every a>=0. For EVERY integer j and ANY lift Phi of geometric Frobenius of F_q, every eigenvalue alpha on gr^M_j(V) is conjectured to be algebraic and have absolute value q^((i+j)/2) under ALL complex embeddings. This is purity of weight i+j. Defining N on an open inertia subgroup does not replace K or q. Finite-extension proof reductions must change cardinality and Frobenius consistently. Extending l-adic coefficients does not change the target. The equivalent source convention compares zero-centred M_j with W_(i+j); weight-filtration existence is not an added unresolved assertion. No restriction to projective, semistable, geometrically connected or special complete-intersection varieties is imposed. l=p, crystalline, torsion and arbitrary rigid-analytic analogues are not substituted.
records.statusQualification: Weight–monodromy remains open_with_solved_subcases. Complete intersections in abelian varieties are a subcase, and 2026 formality work assumes weight–monodromy. Rigid-analytic counterexamples or l=p analogues are not the frozen smooth proper algebraic l != p statement.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Establish universal prescribed Frobenius weights on monodromy-graded proper-smooth cohomology.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Establish failure of the proposed universal local monodromy-purity relation.

records.canonicalTitle: Campana's Conjecture Characterizing Special Varieties by Potential Density of Rational Points
records.exactTarget: For every number field K and every smooth projective geometrically integral variety X/K, prove or disprove that X over an algebraic closure of K is special in Campana's sense if and only if X(L) is Zariski dense in X for some finite extension L/K. Here specialness has its usual projective meaning: for each integer 1<=p<=dim X and rank-one coherent subsheaf F of the sheaf of algebraic p-forms on X over the algebraic closure, the Kodaira dimension kappa(F) is less than p (equivalently, the Campana core is a point). A proof must establish the biconditional for all such X; one counterexample to either implication refutes it. This target excludes nonproper integral-point, weakly-special, analytic and function-field variants.
records.statusQualification: The December 2025 Bartsch–Javanpeykar–Levin paper states that neither implication is known in full generality, and March 2026 discussion retains the arithmetic conjecture while separating weak specialness and geometric results.
records.readerQuestion: For a smooth projective geometrically integral variety over a number field, is Campana's geometric condition of specialness exactly what allows its rational points to become Zariski dense after a finite extension of the field? Specialness is tested over the algebraic closure.
records.familyLabel: Campana specialness and rational points
records.whyItMatters: This would characterize an arithmetic property—potential density of rational points—by geometry. A proof would also give potential density for K3 surfaces and the Bombieri–Lang non-density assertion for positive-dimensional varieties of general type.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would characterize arithmetic potential density geometrically, imply potential density for all K3 surfaces over number fields, and imply Bombieri–Lang non-density for positive-dimensional varieties of general type.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would separate arithmetic potential density from Campana specialness in at least one direction; it would not automatically refute the K3 or Bombieri–Lang assertions.

records.readerQuestion: Can Bose–Einstein condensation be proved for an interacting gas of bosons moving in continuous three-dimensional space at low temperatures? The target is persistent off-diagonal long-range order as particle number and volume grow together at fixed density.

records.canonicalTitle: Grothendieck Standard Conjecture of Hodge Type
records.exactTarget: For every smooth projective irreducible variety X of dimension n over an algebraically closed field k of any characteristic and every ample divisor class L, put N^i(X)_Q equal to codimension-i algebraic cycles with rational coefficients modulo numerical equivalence, with N^j=0 outside 0<=j<=n. For each integer 0<=i<=n/2 let P_L^i=ker(L^(n-2i+1):N^i(X)_Q -> N^(n-i+1)(X)_Q). The numerical standard conjecture of Hodge type asserts that q_L^i(a,b)=(-1)^i deg(a.b.L^(n-2i)) is positive definite on P_L^i after extending scalars to R. This is numerical primitive positivity, not an unconditional identification with primitive algebraic cohomology for an arbitrary Weil theory; it does not assume or require proving the other standard conjectures separately.
records.statusQualification: Standard Conjecture of Hodge type remains open_with_solved_subcases. Fourfolds, powers of threefolds and other specified examples do not establish numerical primitive positivity in every dimension and characteristic; newer preprint proofs were not independently certified.
records.readerQualification: Standard Conjecture of Hodge type remains open, with solved subcases. Fourfolds, powers of threefolds and other specified examples do not establish numerical primitive positivity in every dimension and characteristic; newer preprint proofs were not independently certified.
records.readerQuestion: After identifying algebraic cycles with the same intersection numbers, does the sign-corrected intersection form give a positive value on every nonzero primitive class? This is asked in codimensions up to half the dimension, for every ample class on smooth projective irreducible varieties over algebraically closed fields of any characteristic.
records.familyLabel: Grothendieck’s standard conjectures
records.whyItMatters: A proof would give a positive inner-product structure to these primitive numerical cycle spaces. The conclusion concerns cycles modulo numerical equivalence and does not itself identify them with primitive classes in an arbitrary cohomology theory.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Settle the numerical Hodge-index positivity law for primitive algebraic cycles in the exact all-characteristic scope.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Establish a failure of the numerical primitive positivity law, identifying a limitation of that assertion without automatically resolving another standard conjecture.

records.canonicalTitle: Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture on the Level of Distribution of Primes
records.exactTarget: Prove that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.

records.readerQualification: Elliott–Halberstam remains open unconditionally. A recent implication assumes both GRH and Dirichlet-L pair correlation, while restricted-modulus results do not prove the stated all-moduli maximal-error estimate.
records.readerQuestion: When counting primes in arithmetic progressions, can their distribution errors be controlled for step sizes nearly as large as the counting limit x? Elliott–Halberstam predicts arbitrarily strong logarithmic savings in the sum of the largest errors over residue classes and shorter counting ranges, for step sizes up to x^θ with any 0 < θ < 1.
records.familyLabel: Elliott-Halberstam Conjecture on the Level of Distribution of Primes
records.whyItMatters: A proof would control the combined error in prime distribution across arithmetic progressions for moduli extending to every fixed power below x. The estimate controls the sum of worst errors for each modulus, retaining uniformity over shorter cutoffs.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Would prove that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Would exhibit a counterexample or obstruction to the assertion that for every A > 0 and every 0 < theta < 1, the sum over q <= x^theta of the maximal Chebyshev error |psi(y; q, a) - y/phi(q)| over y <= x and (a,q)=1 is O(x / (log x)^A), extending Bombieri-Vinogradov from theta < 1/2 to every theta < 1.

records.canonicalTitle: PSPACE versus EXPTIME
records.exactTarget: Determine whether PSPACE=EXPTIME for languages over finite binary strings in the standard deterministic multitape Turing-machine model with a read-only input tape and work tapes. PSPACE is the union over integers k>=1 of DSPACE(n^k), with asymptotic constant factors allowed and read-only input cells not counted as work space. EXPTIME is the union over integers k>=1 of DTIME(2^(n^k)), with asymptotic constant factors allowed. Machines are total deciders that halt on every input. This is an unrelativized equality of the full classes, not of one fixed resource exponent.
records.statusQualification: PSPACE versus EXPTIME remains open with bounded recency evidence. The Czerwinski separation was withdrawn in March 2024 with an independent critique, which defeats that claim but does not certify absence of every later one.
records.readerQualification: PSPACE versus EXPTIME remains open with bounded recency evidence. The Czerwinski separation was withdrawn in March 2024 with an independent critique, which defeats that claim but does not certify absence of every later one.
records.readerQuestion: If a deterministic algorithm solves a yes-or-no problem in time 2^(n^k) for some fixed k, must another deterministic algorithm solve it using only polynomially many working-memory bits in the input length n?
records.familyLabel: PSPACE versus EXPTIME
records.whyItMatters: An equality would show that polynomial memory suffices for every computation in the full exponential-time class. A separation would identify a decision problem whose time bound can be exponential but whose memory requirements exceed every polynomial.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Equality would place every deterministic exponential-time decision problem within polynomial work space, though not necessarily polynomial time. This follows directly from the fixed class definitions and the known inclusion.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Strict containment would establish an exponential-time-decidable language requiring more than every polynomial work-space bound, resolving this specific time-versus-space boundary without automatically settling other class separations.

records.canonicalTitle: Grothendieck–Teichmüller Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let G_Q=Gal(Qbar/Q). Let GT-hat be Drinfeld's original profinite Grothendieck-Teichmuller group, including its standard commutator and invertibility conditions, not merely the pair-equation monoid, gentle GT, a pro-l or prounipotent version, or a higher-genus subgroup. Fix the standard Ihara embedding Ih:G_Q -> GT-hat specified by the Ihara splitting in Bortnovskyi-Dolgushev-Holikov-Pashkovskyi Section1.3, equations1.5-1.6: Ih(g)=((chi(g)-1)/2,f_g) in that source's coordinates, with chi the cyclotomic character, and associated action x -> x^chi(g), y -> f_g^(-1)y^chi(g)f_g on the profinite free group. The conjecture asserts that this actual continuous injective homomorphism is surjective, hence an isomorphism of profinite groups. The source's group law and fixed splitting are retained; formulas from an opposite composition convention are not mixed into this definition.
records.statusQualification: Grothendieck–Teichmuller remains open for surjectivity of the fixed Ihara embedding into the original full profinite GT. August 2026 quotient results and underlying-space homeomorphisms do not prove this group-homomorphism surjectivity.
records.readerQualification: Grothendieck–Teichmuller remains open for surjectivity of the fixed Ihara embedding into the original full profinite GT. August 2026 quotient results and underlying-space homeomorphisms do not prove this group-homomorphism surjectivity.
records.readerQuestion: The absolute Galois group of the rationals describes the field symmetries of algebraic numbers. Does its standard Ihara embedding account for every element of Drinfeld’s original profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group, which encodes compatible symmetries of fundamental-group data?
records.familyLabel: Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory
records.whyItMatters: Surjectivity would identify that entire profinite group with the arithmetic Galois group through the actual embedding. Failure would exhibit elements satisfying the group’s defining conditions that do not arise from Galois symmetries.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Identify every element of the original profinite GT as arising under the actual absolute-Galois embedding.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Establish that the original profinite GT contains genuinely nongalois elements, delimiting that group-theoretic reconstruction criterion.

records.canonicalTitle: Entanglement Area Law for 2D Gapped Quantum Systems
records.exactTarget: Prove the two-dimensional ground-state area-law conjecture for finite-dimensional lattice spins: for families of finite 2D square-lattice Hamiltonians with fixed on-site dimension, uniformly bounded finite-range local interactions, a unique ground state, and a positive spectral-gap lower bound independent of system size, the ground-state entanglement entropy S(rho_A) is at most C times the boundary size |partial A| for every region A. The constant C may depend on the fixed local parameters and gap lower bound, but not on the system size or region. Here rho_A is the reduced pure-ground-state density operator and boundary size counts lattice edges crossing from A to its complement.
records.statusQualification: The universal two-dimensional gapped ground-state area law remains open. The 2026 AGSP theorem adds conditions available in restricted frustration-free locally gapped cases, not every globally gapped unique-ground-state Hamiltonian.
records.readerQualification: The universal two-dimensional gapped ground-state area law remains open. The 2026 AGSP theorem adds conditions available in restricted frustration-free locally gapped cases, not every globally gapped unique-ground-state Hamiltonian.
records.readerQuestion: For locally interacting quantum spins on a square lattice, with a unique ground state and a size-independent positive energy gap, must every region’s entanglement entropy be at most a constant times the number of edges crossing its boundary? The constant may depend on the fixed local parameters and gap, but not on the region or lattice size.
records.familyLabel: Entanglement Area Law for 2D Gapped Quantum Systems
records.whyItMatters: A proof would limit entanglement by boundary size throughout this class, including frustrated Hamiltonians. The constant could depend on fixed interaction parameters and the gap, while remaining valid as the system and chosen region grow.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Would establish the boundary-size entropy bound throughout this class, including frustrated Hamiltonians, with constants uniform in system and region size at fixed local parameters and gap lower bound.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Would construct a family in this same finite-spin, bounded finite-range, unique-ground-state, uniformly gapped class for which S(rho_A)/|partial A| is unbounded. Degenerate-ground-space examples, gap-closing families, or failure of a particular proof method do not refute this assertion.

records.canonicalTitle: Deligne's Absolute Hodge Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every smooth projective variety X over C, every p>=0 and every rational Hodge class alpha in H^(2p)(X,Q(p)), alpha is absolute Hodge: for every automorphism sigma of C, its sigma-conjugate under algebraic de Rham comparison on X^sigma is again a rational Hodge class, with the same Tate-twist convention.

records.readerQuestion: Hodge classes are cohomology classes singled out by a variety's complex geometry. On every smooth projective complex variety, must each rational Hodge class remain one after any automorphism of the complex number field?
records.familyLabel: Hodge conjectures
records.whyItMatters: A proof would make the Hodge property invariant under all these field automorphisms, using the specified de Rham comparison and Tate twist. A counterexample would identify a class whose conjugate loses that property.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would establish stability of rational Hodge classes under all complex-field automorphisms.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would refute that stability and, because algebraic classes are absolute, also refute the ordinary Hodge conjecture.

resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would exhibit a real pair whose multiplicative approximation quantity stays bounded away from zero.

records.canonicalTitle: Cohen-Lenstra class-group distributions for quadratic number fields
records.exactTarget: For u in {0,1} let K_u(X) be the set of isomorphism classes of quadratic number fields K with |disc(K)| < X that are imaginary (u = 0) or real (u = 1). For each fixed odd prime p and each finite abelian p-group A, prove that the limit as X tends to infinity of #{K in K_u(X) : Cl(K)[p^infinity] is isomorphic to A} / #K_u(X) exists and equals (1/Z_u(p)) * |A|^{-u} / |Aut(A)|, where Z_u(p) is the sum over isomorphism classes of finite abelian p-groups B of |B|^{-u}/|Aut(B)| (so Z_0(p) = prod_{i>=1}(1-p^{-i})^{-1} and Z_1(p) = prod_{i>=2}(1-p^{-i})^{-1}). Cl(K) is the ordinary ideal class group and Cl(K)[p^infinity] its Sylow p-subgroup. No assertion is made for p = 2, for narrow class groups, for a joint law over several primes, or for any non-quadratic family.

The June survey's original-law discussion and the actual October 2025 Landesman-Levy theorem preserve the distinction between current function-field advances and this target. records.readerQuestion: Class groups measure how unique factorization can fail in number fields. records.whyItMatters: The formula would specify the limiting frequency of every finite abelian p-group in each quadratic family. It would turn a weighting rule into exact statistical predictions for ordinary class groups, separately for real and imaginary fields.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof establishes the stated asymptotic frequencies for every fixed finite odd-primary group in each family, including the predicted frequency of class numbers not divisible by a fixed odd prime. Because every stated group weight is positive, each such group occurs infinitely often. records.canonicalTitle: Serre's congruence subgroup conjecture
records.exactTarget: Let K be a global field (a number field or the function field of a curve over a finite field), G an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic K-group, and S a finite nonempty set of places of K containing every archimedean place when K is a number field. Put r_S(G) = sum over v in S of rank_{K_v}(G), and let C^S(G) be the kernel of the natural surjection from the profinite completion of G(O_S) (S-arithmetic topology) onto its S-congruence completion. Prove Serre's congruence subgroup conjecture: (a) if r_S(G) >= 2 and rank_{K_v}(G) > 0 for every nonarchimedean v in S, then C^S(G) is finite; (b) if r_S(G) = 1, then C^S(G) is infinite. The case r_S(G) = 0 (finite G(O_S), trivial kernel) is excluded. Finiteness of C^S(G) is the assertion; triviality is a stronger statement not required. Which specific groups remain unsettled is status information, not part of the target.

The new 2026 paper explicitly states unresolved finite-S quaternion cases and its theorem has an infinite-S hypothesis. The bounded sweep and proof-reading limits remain explicit. records.readerQuestion: For arithmetic groups arising from simply connected, absolutely almost simple algebraic groups, is the congruence kernel—the gap between finite-quotient and congruence information—finite in total rank at least two when all selected nonarchimedean local ranks are positive, but infinite in rank one?
records.familyLabel: Serre's congruence subgroup conjecture
records.whyItMatters: The kernel measures the discrepancy between two ways of recovering an arithmetic group from finite information. A proof would classify that discrepancy as finite or infinite under these rank hypotheses, without requiring finite kernels to be trivial.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: The proof establishes the qualitative finite/infinite classification under the selected rank hypotheses, completing this aspect of the comparison between arithmetic and congruence completions. It need not compute any finite kernel or make every finite-index subgroup a congruence subgroup.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: An admissible counterexample shows that these rank and local-isotropy conditions do not suffice for the proposed dichotomy. It need not identify a replacement classification or explain the entire obstruction. A finite nontrivial higher-rank kernel is not a counterexample.

records.canonicalTitle: Regular Inverse Galois Problem over Q

records.familyLabel: Inverse Galois over Q
records.whyItMatters: Such realizations would supply geometric covers for every finite group. Hilbert irreducibility would then give every finite group as a Galois group over Q, settling ordinary inverse Galois affirmatively.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would provide regular covers over Q for every finite group and, by Hilbert irreducibility, prove the ordinary inverse Galois assertion over Q.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would exhibit an obstruction to regular realization over Q(T); it need not refute ordinary inverse Galois over Q.

records.canonicalTitle: Murre's Chow-Kunneth Conjectures
records.exactTarget: For every smooth projective irreducible complex variety X of dimension d, let CH^j(X)_Q denote cycles modulo rational equivalence, with Betti Q-cohomology. A correspondence pi in CH^d(X x X)_Q acts by pi_*(a)=(p_2)_*(p_1^*(a).pi). Murre's full A-D package asserts: (A) there exists a Chow-Kunneth decomposition, namely mutually orthogonal composition-idempotents pi_0,...,pi_(2d) in CH^d(X x X)_Q summing to the diagonal and inducing projection onto H^i(X,Q) for pi_i; (B) for EVERY such decomposition and 0<=j<=d, pi_i acts as zero on CH^j when i<j or i>2j; (C) for EVERY such decomposition define F^r CH^j as the intersection of ker(pi_i)_* for max(0,2j-r+1)<=i<=2j, r>=0, with empty intersection F^0=CH^j; these filtrations are equal for ALL decompositions satisfying A; (D) for EVERY such decomposition, F^1 CH^j equals ker(CH^j(X)_Q -> H^(2j)(X,Q)). Under A and B, F^(j+1)=0. No multiplicative or self-dual decomposition, explicit construction algorithm, functorial-extra requirement, or arbitrary-base-field enlargement is included.

Define lambda:R tensor U->R tensor X by lambda(u)=-sum_w log|u|_w w, using product-formula normalized absolute values. For each irreducible complex character chi of G, set R_S(chi,f)=det_C(lambda f acting by postcomposition on Hom_C[G](V_(dual chi),C tensor X)) and A_S(chi,f)=R_S(chi,f)/L_S^*(0,chi), where L_S^* is the first nonzero Laurent coefficient of the S-truncated Artin L-function and an empty determinant is1. records.canonicalTitle: Inhomogeneous Landau–Coulomb Global Regularity (HST All-Moment Data)
records.exactTarget: Fix a positive physical constant a. On [0,infinity) times R^3_x times R^3_v consider the classical Landau equation (partial_t+v dot grad_x)f=Q(f,f), where Q(f,f)=div_v integral_{R^3} A(v-w)[f(t,x,w) grad_v f(t,x,v)-f(t,x,v) grad_w f(t,x,w)]dw and A(z)=a |z|^(-1)(I-z tensor z/|z|^2) for z!=0. For every nonnegative initial datum f_0 on R^6 with f_0 in the global Holder space C^alpha for some 0<alpha<1, sup_{x,v}<v>^k f_0(x,v)<infinity for every k>=0, and constants delta,r_0,R>0 such that for every x there exists |v_x|<R with f_0>=delta on the Euclidean R^6 ball B_{r_0}(x,v_x), does the classical solution branch constructed in HST Theorems 1.2–1.4 have maximal continuation time T_E=infinity? Here <v>=(1+|v|^2)^(1/2); the branch matches f_0 as t decreases to zero, is smooth for positive time, and has all polynomial velocity weights bounded on every finite time slab of its existence. The exact question is global extension of that branch, with the sufficiently decaying uniformly continuous kinetic weak uniqueness convention in HST Section 5, not uniqueness among all generalized weak solutions. The HST Coulomb continuation quantity is Psi(T)=esssup_{0<=t<=T,x} integral f(t,x,v)dv + esssup_{0<=t<=T,x,v} f(t,x,v). Finite Psi on every finite time slab is the associated continuation criterion, not an extra hypothesis presumed true. No smallness near equilibrium, finite total spatial mass or uniform bound across different initial data is imposed.

records.canonicalTitle: Voevodsky's Smash-Nilpotence Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field k, every smooth projective k-variety X of dimension d, every integer 0<=r<=d, and every class alpha in CH^r(X)_Q (codimension-r cycles modulo rational equivalence with rational coefficients), assume deg(alpha.beta)=0 for every beta in CH^(d-r)(X)_Q. Voevodsky's smash-nilpotence assertion is that there exists an integer N>=1, depending on alpha, for which the N-fold EXTERNAL product alpha times ... times alpha is zero in CH^(Nr)(X^N)_Q, where X^N is the fibre product over k. No algebraic-closure, characteristic-zero or geometric-connectedness hypothesis is imposed; disconnected smooth projective schemes are interpreted on their pure-dimensional components. The reverse implication, smash-nilpotent implies numerically trivial, is known, so this is equality of numerical and smash equivalence for rational cycles. Neither intersection powers on X, composition powers of correspondences, integral coefficients, nor a uniform or computable exponent replaces this assertion.

It supplies the hypotheses of Cesnavicius Proposition3.1.5 for uniqueness up to isomorphism of reductive group models with fixed generic fiber. This is neither uniqueness of an isomorphism nor existence of every extension, and it does not by itself settle the separate purity image or Bass–Quillen conjectures.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: One admissible nontrivial generically trivial torsor refutes the universal assertion and forces a limit on that local-to-generic principle. A counterexample on a singular ring or for a nonreductive group does not suffice. No failure of every known subcase, every reductive model uniqueness statement or all purity assertions is inferred.

records.canonicalTitle: Palis finite-attractor full-basin density conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold M and every finite integer r >= 1, prove the conjunction of the following two density assertions: (i) in Diff^r(M) with its C^r topology there is a dense subset D whose elements f have finitely many attractors whose basins of attraction together cover M up to a set of smooth-volume measure zero; (ii) the same holds in the space X^r(M) of C^r vector fields with its C^r topology, for the attractors and basins of the generated flows. Attractor follows Palis (2005) Sections 2.1 and 2.3: a compact invariant set A that is transitive (has a dense orbit) and attracts a set of positive volume, its basin being the set of points whose forward orbit (or forward flow trajectory) converges to A. The finite number of attractors may depend on the element of D; no uniform bound is required. Volume-zero is independent of the choice of smooth positive density on M. This is the first bullet of Palis's Global Conjecture only; physical measures, stochastic stability, metric stability under parameter perturbation, and one-dimensional-family statements are separate conjectures not included.

It supplies an approximation-level description of possible asymptotic accumulation, not a theorem about Lebesgue-typical parameters, convergent time averages, physical measures, stochastic stability or reliable numerical forecasting.

records.canonicalTitle: Effective Roth Theorem

records.readerQuestion: For any real irrational root α of an integer polynomial and any positive rational ε, can an algorithm compute a denominator cutoff beyond which no reduced fraction p/q satisfies |α−p/q|<1/q^(2+ε)?
records.familyLabel: Effective Roth Theorem
records.whyItMatters: Such an algorithm would make the entire finite set of exceptionally close rational approximations computable from the inputs. Its existence would not promise practical runtime or a reasonably sized bound.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Would make the entire finite exceptional set of reduced rational approximations computable for every algebraic input and positive rational epsilon. resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Would separate qualitative finiteness of each Roth exceptional set from existence of a single total algorithm uniformly bounding these sets. It would not contradict Roth's theorem or assert that individual exceptional sets are infinite or noncomputable.

records.canonicalTitle: Morton–Silverman Uniform Boundedness Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For all fixed integers N>=1, d>=2 and D>=1, there exists a finite constant C(N,d,D) such that for every number field K with [K:Q]<=D and every degree-d K-morphism phi:P^N_K->P^N_K, the set of K-rational preperiodic points has cardinality at most C(N,d,D). A point is preperiodic when its forward orbit under phi is finite. The morphism is everywhere defined, equivalently given by homogeneous degree-d forms with no common projective zero. The bound is independent of the field and map except for N,d,D; no effective formula or classification is required.
records.statusQualification: Rajagopal–Zhang's July2026version explicitly leaves full periodic uniformity conjectural while proving a polynomial result with inseparable good reduction. records.readerQuestion: Under repeated application of an algebraic map on projective space, some rational points eventually repeat. Is their number uniformly bounded once the dimension, the map's degree and the degree of its number field are bounded? The map must be defined everywhere and have degree at least two.
records.familyLabel: Morton–Silverman Uniform Boundedness Conjecture
records.whyItMatters: A proof would bound finite rational orbits uniformly across all maps and fields with those parameters. A counterexample would show unbounded orbit-point counts even while the three parameters remain fixed.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Uniform projective preperiodic boundedness would hold across each fixed-parameter class. Fakhruddin's extension construction and Zarhin's trick give torsion-cardinality bounds depending only on abelian dimension and field degree, hence the admitted all-g>=2 fixed-field assertion. No numerical embedding formula, effective uniform bound, converse or family-standing clearance is asserted.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Unbounded preperiodic cardinalities at one fixed triple refute the universal assertion without contradicting individual-map finiteness or the restricted good-reduction theorems. Failure of this stronger assertion would not itself refute its abelian-torsion consequence. Periodic-only claims need a checked settling implication; logical nonequivalence is not assumed.

records.canonicalTitle: Perfect-Matching Search in Deterministic NC (General Graphs)

Here F is the centered real stationary isotropic Gaussian field with covariance E[F(x)F(y)]=integral_{S^{d-1}} cos(<x-y,theta>) d sigma(theta), where sigma is probability surface measure on the unit sphere (unit variance and unit spectral radius, no extra 2*pi factor).

records.canonicalTitle: Zagier's dimension conjecture for classical multiple zeta values
records.exactTarget: For positive integers k_1,...,k_r with k_1>=2, define the classical convergent real multiple zeta value zeta(k_1,...,k_r)=sum_(n_1>...>n_r>0) 1/(n_1^k_1 ... n_r^k_r), of weight k_1+...+k_r. For each k>=2 let Z_k be their Q-linear span at weight k, with Z_0=Q generated by the empty value1 and Z_1={0}. Define d_0=1,d_1=0,d_2=1 and d_k=d_(k-2)+d_(k-3) for k>=3. Is dim_Q Z_k=d_k for every k>=0?
records.statusQualification: The classical weightwise dimension equality remains open in the bounded source review. The known upper bound and Brown's motivic Hoffman basis give numerical spanning, not the missing universal lower bound. Machide's formal characteristic2 computations through22 do not settle numerical independence. records.readerQuestion: Multiple zeta values are nested infinite sums, grouped by the sum k of their exponents, called their weight. Is the number d_k of rationally independent values at each weight governed by d_k=d_(k−2)+d_(k−3), with d_0=1, d_1=0 and d_2=1?
records.familyLabel: Zagier's dimension conjecture for classical multiple zeta values
records.whyItMatters: A proof would count the independent multiple zeta values separately at each weight. It would determine exactly how many numbers are needed to express all values of that weight by rational linear combinations.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would determine every classical weightwise rational dimension and show that the numerical Hoffman {2,3} spanning values form a basis in each weight. It would not alone establish independence across different weights or every general period conjecture.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would reveal an additional numerical rational relation beyond those compatible with the motivic Hoffman basis at some weight, giving a kernel in that weight's period map. It would not refute the motivic basis theorem or automatically every formal double-shuffle statement.

records.readerQuestion: The quotient Salvetti construction builds a standard space from an Artin group's defining Coxeter system. For every such system with finitely many generators, is this space's universal cover contractible, making it a classifying space for the group?
records.familyLabel: Geometry and topology of Artin groups
records.whyItMatters: A proof would validate this explicit topological model for every Artin group in the stated class. Its universal cover would be contractible, leaving the fundamental group as its only nontrivial homotopy group.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof supplies the finite quotient Salvetti space as a classifying space for every finite-rank Artin group, implies torsion-freeness and the center conjecture, and makes this model available for group-cohomological calculations. No general efficient word-problem algorithm is asserted.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample shows that the standard quotient Salvetti model has nontrivial higher homotopy for some Artin group, so that model fails to be its classifying space. records.canonicalTitle: Reliability Function of the Binary Symmetric Channel Below the Critical Rate
records.exactTarget: Determine the optimal fixed-blocklength reliability function of the memoryless binary symmetric channel without feedback for every crossover probability 0<p<1/2 and every rate 0<R<R_crit(p). With equiprobable messages, let P_e^*(n,R,p) be the minimum average block error under maximum-likelihood decoding among binary length-n codes of cardinality at least ceil(2^(nR)). Define E(R,p)=limsup_{n->infinity}[-log_2 P_e^*(n,R,p)]/n. Here H_2 is binary entropy and R_crit(p)=1-H_2(sqrt(p)/(sqrt(p)+sqrt(1-p))). Success requires matching achievable and converse exponents, or an equivalent evaluable exact characterization, for all these parameters. Restating the operational optimization or merely improving unmatched bounds is not a resolution.

records.readerQuestion: When each transmitted bit independently flips with probability 0<p<1/2 and there is no feedback, what is the best asymptotic exponent of average block-error decay? Determine it for fixed-blocklength codes at every positive rate below the channel's critical rate, optimizing over all codes with equally likely messages. Use the limsup of −log₂(error)/block length.

records.whyItMatters: An exact answer would identify the optimal tradeoff between information rate and error decay in this basic noisy channel. It would provide a performance benchmark; an efficient encoding or decoding algorithm would be a separate achievement.

resolutionConsequences.completeResolution: A complete determination would identify the optimal asymptotic tradeoff between rate and block-error decay for the binary symmetric channel below its critical rate, supplying a performance benchmark without automatically producing an efficient encoder or decoder.

records.canonicalTitle: Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field K of characteristic zero, every quasiprojective variety X over K, every K-morphism f:X->X, every closed K-subvariety V of X and every point x in X(K), the set {n in Z_{≥0}: f^n(x) is in V(K)} is a finite union of arithmetic progressions {a+bm:m in Z_{≥0}} with a,b nonnegative integers. A zero step b=0 permits a singleton, and an empty union permits no returns. All iterates are defined because f is a morphism. No dominance, etaleness, smoothness, automorphism or degree restriction is imposed.
records.statusQualification: The2026primary introductions distinguish the full conjecture from etale, specified affine-plane and split-curve theorems. XYZ's product corollary has additional factor hypotheses and only DML(1) scope. A search-summary assertion of full resolution is not source evidence. Bounded review does not attest the absence of all other claims. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.
records.readerQuestion: Repeatedly apply an algebraic map to a point and record when its orbit lands in a fixed algebraic subvariety. In characteristic zero, are these return times always a finite union of arithmetic progressions and isolated times, for every everywhere-defined map of a quasiprojective variety?
records.familyLabel: Dynamical Mordell–Lang Conjecture
records.whyItMatters: A proof would force these orbit-intersection times to follow finitely many recurring schedules with finitely many isolated exceptions. A counterexample would reveal a return-time pattern outside that arithmetic structure.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Every admissible return set would decompose into finitely many progressions, including singleton exceptions. The survey's periodic-subvariety consequence requires a wandering orbit and infinitely many distinct intersection points, and uses f^m(Z) contained in Z. The assertion alone does not provide an effective decomposition, a Skolem algorithm or a converse from mere periodic-subvariety existence.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: One rigorously established admissible return set lacking every such finite decomposition refutes the universal assertion. Positive-characteristic phenomena or partially defined rational maps do not suffice. Existing etale and specified other theorems remain valid; no failure of all arithmetic dynamical structure follows.

records.canonicalTitle: RL versus L
records.exactTarget: Let L be the languages of binary strings decided by deterministic Turing machines using O(log(N+2)) work space on length-N inputs. Let RL use the same read-only input and read-write work-tape convention but allow fresh unbiased read-once random bits, retaining an old bit only by storing it in counted work space. The machine must halt for every input and every random tape, use O(log(N+2)) work space, accept each yes input with probability at least2/3, and accept each no input with probability0. records.readerQuestion: Can randomness be removed from every always-halting decision algorithm that uses only logarithmic working memory, never says yes when the answer is no, and says yes with probability at least two-thirds when the answer is yes? The replacement must also use only logarithmic working memory.
records.familyLabel: Derandomizing logarithmic space
records.whyItMatters: Equality would eliminate randomness from every decision problem in this one-sided-error model without changing the logarithmic space bound. A separation would establish a workspace advantage for randomness under these exact rules.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Equality would remove randomness from every one-sided-error logarithmic-workspace decision algorithm with only constant-factor work-space overhead in the selected halting model. It would not newly solve undirected connectivity, and it does not by itself assert the stronger BPL=L equality.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Separation would establish a genuine workspace advantage for fresh randomness with one-sided error on at least one language. It would preclude a universal deterministic-logspace simulation for this model, without separating L from every neighboring randomized or nondeterministic class individually.

records.canonicalTitle: MAJORITY is not in ACC0
records.exactTarget: Let MAJORITY_n(x)=1 exactly when sum_i x_i>=n/2. Define nonuniform ACC0 as Boolean families computed, for every input length n>=1, by circuits of polynomial size and some fixed constant depth using unbounded-fan-in AND, OR and MOD_m gates and fan-in-one NOT gates, with constants allowed and one fixed integer modulus m>=2 across all lengths; MOD_m outputs1 exactly when the input sum is divisible by m. Size counts input and internal gates; depth counts gate layers. The depth, modulus and polynomial size bound may depend on the family, not on n. Is the family (MAJORITY_n) outside ACC0?
records.statusQualification: Krishan–Vishwanathan's July2026 paper explicitly retains majority nonmembership as Conjecture1 and gives an LP reformulation and partial degree results. Williams' NEXP circuit lower bound and BHLR's symmetric torus results do not settle this easily computable Boolean function.
