records.readerQuestion: Can majority—whether at least half the input bits are one—ever be computed by polynomial-size Boolean circuits with a fixed number of layers, using AND, OR, NOT and gates testing divisibility of their input count by one fixed modulus? The AND, OR and divisibility gates may take arbitrarily many inputs.
records.familyLabel: MAJORITY is not in ACC0
records.whyItMatters: A proof would establish a circuit-size limitation for this explicit counting task, across every fixed depth and modulus. A negative answer would show that a shallow modular circuit family can compute majority.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would give an unconditional superpolynomial ACC0 lower bound for a concrete, efficiently computable threshold function, separating its computation from every fixed-depth fixed-modulus polynomial-size family. It would not follow merely from an unrelated NP or NEXP noncontainment theorem.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would show that constant-depth modular Boolean circuits of polynomial size suffice for majority, overturning this lower-bound conjecture. This does not itself supply a uniform generator, a proof about P versus NP, or a cryptographic algorithm.

records.canonicalTitle: Kuznetsov Rationality Conjecture for Cubic Fourfolds
records.exactTarget: For every smooth cubic fourfold X contained in P^5_C, let Ku(X) be the full right-orthogonal subcategory of D^b(coh X) consisting of objects E with Hom(O_X(i),E[j])=0 for i=0,1,2 and all integers j. The Kuznetsov rationality conjecture asserts: X is rational, meaning birational over C to P^4_C, if and only if there exists a smooth projective complex K3 surface S and an exact C-linear triangulated equivalence Ku(X) ~= D^b(coh S). The K3 category is untwisted: no nonzero chosen Brauer twist is permitted; this does not require Br(S)=0. No polarization, marking, chosen kernel, explicit algorithm or separately imposed Fourier-Mukai condition is added. The assertion quantifies over ALL smooth complex cubic fourfolds, not only general points of a special divisor.

records.canonicalTitle: Zagier Conjecture on Dedekind Zeta Values
records.exactTarget: For every number field F of signature (r1,r2) and every integer k>=2, put n=r2 for even k and n=r1+r2 for odd k. There exist xi_1,...,xi_n in A_k(F) tensor Q, using the allowable-symbol group defined by Zagier--Gangl section2, such that zeta_F(k) belongs to Q^times times sqrt(abs(D_F)) pi^{k([F:Q]-n)} det(L_k(sigma_i(xi_j)))_{1<=i,j<=n}. Here L_k is the single-valued polylogarithm defined there by the Bernoulli-number combination of classical polylogarithms (imaginary part for even k, real part for odd k), extended Q-linearly to symbols. For even k take one embedding from each conjugate complex pair; for odd k also take all real embeddings. The empty determinant is1. This is existence of the determinant formula, not the stronger regulator-lattice or Bloch-group rank assertion.

records.whyItMatters: A positive answer would make graphs with this logarithmic avoidance guarantee uniformly constructible in time polynomial in their size. It would produce the entire adjacency matrix, without requiring faster individual adjacency queries.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would make the probabilistic logarithmic clique/independence order attainable by ordinary uniform polynomial-time graph production. It would close this explicit-versus-existence gap without necessarily giving an optimal extractor or strongly explicit adjacency oracle.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would separate efficient uniform graph production from the known nonconstructive logarithmic Ramsey existence theorem. It must rule out all polynomial-time constructions, not merely algebraic or extractor-based approaches.

records.canonicalTitle: Grigorchuk Gap Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every finitely generated group G with finite generating set X, let gamma_G,X(n) count elements of word length at most n in X union X^(-1). For positive functions on positive integers, write f preceq g if some integer C>=1 satisfies f(n)<=C g(Cn) for every n>=1, and f prec g if f preceq g but not g preceq f. Prove that gamma_G,X prec exp(sqrt(n)) implies that G has polynomial growth, equivalently that G is virtually nilpotent. The growth comparison is independent of the finite generating set. It is strict comparison of growth classes, not merely an eventual numerical upper bound or non-strict domination.
records.statusQualification: The selected primary papers state the general one-half conjecture, and the November 2025 preprint reports only smaller-exponent progress within a restricted class. The bounded September 7 search found no accepted proof or counterexample for the exact all-finitely-generated-groups statement. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.
records.readerQuestion: Count the elements of a finitely generated group reachable in at most n generator steps. If this growth is strictly below exp(√n), when growth rates are compared up to constant rescaling of n and value, must it actually be bounded by a polynomial?
records.familyLabel: Grigorchuk Gap Conjecture
records.whyItMatters: A proof would exclude intermediate growth throughout this strict region and force such groups to be virtually nilpotent. A counterexample would place nonpolynomial growth below the proposed boundary.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution rules out non-polynomial group growth strictly below the proposed boundary class and extends the structural force of polynomial-growth theory to that whole strict region.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution supplies an intermediate-growth group below the proposed boundary and overturns the asserted universal gap, without automatically classifying the full spectrum of growth rates.

records.canonicalTitle: Kaplansky's Idempotent Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every field K of arbitrary characteristic and every torsion-free group G, prove that each idempotent e in the ordinary scalar group ring K[G] is 0 or 1. Here K[G] consists of finite formal K-linear combinations of elements of G, with the group multiplication extended bilinearly, and idempotent means e^2=e. The group need not be finitely generated. This is not a claim that matrix rings over K[G], completed operator algebras or integral quandle rings have no nontrivial idempotents.
records.statusQualification: The universal idempotent assertion remains classified open in this bounded September 7 review, supported directly by the primary scalar-problem discussions. Gardam refutes units, not idempotents; the September 2026 quandle result concerns a different algebra. No accepted scalar field-group-ring resolution was located. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.
records.readerQuestion: Form finite linear combinations of elements of a torsion-free group, using coefficients in any field. Are zero and one the only combinations that stay unchanged when squared? Torsion-free means that no nonidentity group element has finite order.
records.familyLabel: Kaplansky’s group ring conjectures
records.whyItMatters: A proof would forbid nontrivial scalar idempotents uniformly across these group rings. A counterexample would also produce nonzero zero divisors, since a nontrivial idempotent satisfies e(1−e)=0.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A positive resolution rules out nontrivial scalar projections in all permitted group rings and fixes one classical algebraic consequence of torsion-freeness across arbitrary fields.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A negative resolution gives an unexpected nontrivial idempotent in a torsion-free scalar group ring and, through e(1-e)=0, also supplies nontrivial zero divisors in that same ring.

Knots are taken up to ambient isotopy respecting their orientation, so a knot and its reverse are included when they are distinct oriented knot types. Extend v linearly from the free abelian group on oriented knot types to singular knots by the usual alternating positive/negative crossing-resolution relation; order at most d means vanishing on every singular knot with d+1 transverse double points. The coefficient group and finite order may depend on the pair. Rational-valued, integer-valued and Kontsevich-injectivity variants are related but are not asserted equivalent here.

records.canonicalTitle: Global Attractor Conjecture for Complex-Balanced Mass-Action Systems
records.exactTarget: For every finite chemical reaction network with positive rate constants and mass-action kinetics that admits a strictly positive complex-balanced equilibrium, let S be the span of its reaction vectors. For every x0 in the strictly positive orthant, prove that the solution starting at x0 converges as t tends to infinity to the unique positive equilibrium in (x0+S) intersected with the strictly positive orthant; or construct such a system and positive initial condition for which this convergence fails. Complex balance means that at each complex total incoming reaction flux equals total outgoing reaction flux at the equilibrium. No boundedness assumption is imposed on the whole stoichiometric compatibility class.
records.statusQualification: Craciun’s 2015/2016 preprint claims a general proof, while Feliu–Shiu in 2025 describe an outline and awaited continuation and Craciun’s 2026 Oxford abstracts still describe the conjecture and proof progress; the status remains claimed_pending_refereeing rather than solved.
records.readerQuestion: In every finite mass-action reaction network with positive rate constants and a strictly positive complex-balanced equilibrium, must every strictly positive initial state converge to the unique positive equilibrium in its stoichiometric compatibility class? Complex balance equates incoming and outgoing flux at each reaction complex; the whole compatibility class need not be bounded.
records.familyLabel: Mass-action persistence and attraction
records.whyItMatters: A proof would turn complex balance into a universal guarantee of eventual relaxation to equilibrium for positive initial concentrations. A counterexample would identify a limitation of that stability principle.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would guarantee global relaxation to the unique positive equilibrium within each positive compatibility class for every complex-balanced mass-action system.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would show that complex balance and its interior entropy Lyapunov function do not suffice for global attraction, exposing an obstruction at the boundary.

records.canonicalTitle: Birkhoff Conjecture (Near-Boundary Continuous Invariant Foliation)
records.exactTarget: For every bounded planar billiard domain Omega whose boundary is a C-infinity simple closed curve with everywhere positive curvature, let T be its usual specular-reflection billiard map on the open phase cylinder M=(R/LZ) x (0,pi), where s is boundary arclength and delta is the incoming angle with the tangent. Suppose an open annular neighborhood U of the grazing end delta=0 is foliated by continuous simple closed T-invariant curves, each essential in M and winding once around the cylinder; U and its foliation are invariant under T. Here neighborhood of that end means U contains (R/LZ) x (0,eta) for some eta>0, with no fixed lower bound on eta or on the rotation numbers reached by the foliation. Assert that the boundary of Omega is an ellipse, with circles included. No central symmetry, closeness to an ellipse, period-four caustic or extension of the foliation to the whole phase cylinder is assumed. The invariant-curve formulation is selected directly; an unproved equivalence to a caustic, rational, measurable or polynomial-integral formulation is not part of the target.

records.canonicalTitle: Original Dubrovin conjecture for Fano manifolds

The explicit Gamma-class formula for C' (Gamma Conjecture II) and the Hodge-Tate refined versions are not part of this target.
records.statusQualification: Clear as open for the full original assertion at review date. The current July reformulation retains the categorical realization as a condition; the newly found June strategy theorem lists convergence, Gamma-I, region, collection and asymptotic hypotheses and gives a del-Pezzo application. records.readerQuestion: On a smooth complex projective Fano manifold, can curve counting and the organization of algebraic sheaves reveal the same structure? records.whyItMatters: A proof would connect quantum cohomology to categorical generation, with Stokes entries given by Euler pairings and the central connection matrix factored through modified Chern characters. The other factor must commute with cup product by c₁; the stronger Gamma-class formula is separate.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof links generic semisimplicity to categorical generation and realizes the selected Stokes data as Euler pairings of an exceptional collection, with the prescribed commuting-factor relation for the central matrix. This does not determine the unspecified operator C', prove Gamma II, provide a complete reconstruction algorithm for Gromov-Witten invariants, or certify homological mirror symmetry.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: An in-scope failure identifies a limit of this particular relation between big quantum cohomology, exceptional collections and monodromy. It may concern the qualitative equivalence or the impossibility of realizing the two identities. It need not refute every mirror-symmetry prediction, and a failure only of a refined Gamma formula is insufficient.

records.exactTarget: For every closed connected orientable surface S of genus g≥3 and every finite-index subgroup H of its orientation-preserving mapping class group Mod(S), there exists a finite-index characteristic subgroup N of π1(S) such that ker(Mod(S)→Out(π1(S)/N)) is contained in H.

records.canonicalTitle: Koebe circle-domain uniformization conjecture
records.exactTarget: For every nonempty connected open domain Omega of the Riemann sphere, there exist a circle domain D in the Riemann sphere and a conformal homeomorphism Omega -> D. A circle domain means a nonempty connected open set each of whose complementary components is a closed round disk or a point. Allow arbitrary connectivity, including uncountably many complementary components and point components; the whole sphere (empty complement) and a sphere minus one point are included as trivial circle-domain cases. Conformal homeomorphism means a bijective conformal map, not a possibly noninjective holomorphic covering. No uniqueness, Mobius rigidity, quantitative distortion, explicit construction or boundary-extension requirement is appended. The universal statement is retained, not replaced by only an uncountable-connectivity or otherwise difficult subclass.
records.statusQualification: The March2026 survey explicitly retains the general conjecture as open and separates restricted existence from uniqueness. records.whyItMatters: A proof would supply circle-domain models even when there are uncountably many complementary components. It would establish existence of such models without asserting their uniqueness or a method for constructing them.

resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Exhibit a limit to circle-domain conformal uniformization in its universal scope, without conflating it with a failure of uniqueness.

records.canonicalTitle: Corona problem for the unit polydisc
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=2 and every finite integer m>=1, let f_1,...,f_m be scalar bounded holomorphic functions on the unit polydisc D^n={z in C^n: |z_k|<1 for all k}. If inf_{z in D^n} sum_{j=1}^m |f_j(z)|>0, then there exist scalar bounded holomorphic g_1,...,g_m on D^n such that sum_{j=1}^m f_j g_j=1 identically. No boundary extension, regularity, operator inequality or sharp solution-norm bound is required. Equivalently, for every n>=2, point evaluations from D^n are dense in the maximal ideal space of H-infinity(D^n).

records.readerQuestion: On a product of two or more complex unit disks, suppose finitely many bounded holomorphic functions never all become arbitrarily small together. Can bounded holomorphic multipliers always make the sum of their products exactly one?

records.whyItMatters: A proof would establish scalar bounded holomorphic Bézout solvability on every such polydisc. It would guarantee existence of coefficients, without requiring boundary regularity or a sharp bound on their norms.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Extend scalar bounded holomorphic Bezout solvability from the disc to every finite-dimensional unit polydisc, equivalently eliminate its maximal-ideal-space corona. No algorithmic, sharp quantitative or external-application guarantee is added.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Establish a genuine maximal-ideal-space corona in some unit polydisc despite the finite tuple's uniform lower bound, limiting that extension of one-variable theory. An existence proof suffices; no requirement of an explicit formula or construction is imposed.

records.canonicalTitle: Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture
records.exactTarget: Every finite loopless multigraph G that is 4-edge-connected admits a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow: there exist an orientation D of E(G) and a function f:E(G)->{-2,-1,1,2} such that at each vertex the sum of f on incoming edges equals the sum on outgoing edges. Four-edge-connected means G remains connected after deletion of any set of at most3 edges. Parallel edges are allowed. Trivial one-vertex loopless graphs have the empty flow. This is the ordinary zero-boundary flow assertion, not the stronger claim of realizing every admissible prescribed boundary modulo3.
records.statusQualification: The general four-edge-connected assertion is classified open. The reviewed sources report the six-edge-connected theorem and planar/projective-planar cases. The March2026 abstract concerns only Cayley graphs on solvable groups of order2n with n square-free. Inaccessible original proofs and this abstract have not been independently proof-checked. records.readerQuestion: Can every finite loopless multigraph remaining connected after deletion of up to three edges be oriented and assigned edge flows of one or two units, with inflow equaling outflow at every vertex?
records.familyLabel: Tutte's 3-Flow Conjecture
records.whyItMatters: A proof would make four-edge-connectivity sufficient for a nowhere-zero integer 3-flow, even with parallel edges. A counterexample would identify a graph whose connectivity does not permit this bounded circulation.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof gives a uniform four-edge-connectivity condition sufficient for a nonzero bounded integer circulation, settling the ordinary three-flow threshold proposed by Tutte.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof identifies a four-edge-connected obstruction to ordinary bounded integer circulation and requires revision of that proposed sufficient condition; a prescribed-boundary obstruction alone would not do so.

records.canonicalTitle: Arithmeticity of Lattices in PU(n,1) for n at Least 4
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=4, every lattice Γ in PU(n,1), the group of holomorphic isometries of complex hyperbolic n-space, is arithmetic. A lattice is a discrete subgroup of finite Haar covolume; both compact and noncompact finite-volume quotients and groups with torsion are included. Arithmeticity has its usual commensurability meaning via arithmetic subgroups of algebraic groups over Q projected through a compact-kernel real-group homomorphism, equivalently after the finite central lift to SU(n,1). No restriction to reflection lattices or one particular arithmetic construction is imposed. Here n is complex dimension, not real rank.
records.statusQualification: Parker and Deraux leave the full question open; BFMS's2023introduction explicitly does likewise after its conditional geometric arithmeticity theorem. Root's two current discovery queries found no full-scope resolution within their bounded results. Dated commensurability counts, snippets and crawl dates are not a2026status inventory; no exhaustive claim clearance or proof audit is asserted. records.readerQuestion: In complex dimension at least four, must every discrete symmetry group giving a finite-volume quotient of complex hyperbolic space be arithmetic, arising from number-theoretic constructions? Compact and noncompact quotients, including groups with torsion, are all included.
records.familyLabel: Arithmeticity of Lattices in PU(n,1) for n at Least 4
records.whyItMatters: A proof would place all these finite-volume complex-hyperbolic lattices within arithmetic commensurability constructions. A single nonarithmetic example in an admissible dimension would refute the universal assertion.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: All admissible lattices would fall within arithmetic commensurability constructions, ruling out nonarithmetic examples for every n>=4. This does not classify or enumerate all arithmetic lattices, establish every possible superrigidity statement, or resolve the distinct closed-geodesics problem.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: One admissible nonarithmetic lattice in a single n>=4would refute universal arithmeticity and extend known existence beyond dimensions2and3. It would not prove such examples exist in every higher dimension, an infinitude of commensurability classes, or a general hybrid construction.

records.canonicalTitle: Dixmier unitarisability problem for discrete groups
records.exactTarget: Every unitarisable discrete group G is amenable. Here unitarisable means: for every complex Hilbert space H and every group representation pi:G->GL(H) by bounded invertible linear operators with sup_{g in G} ||pi(g)||<infinity in operator norm, there exists a bounded invertible S on H such that S pi(g) S^{-1} is unitary for all g. There is no countability or Hilbert-space separability restriction. Equivalently, every nonamenable discrete group admits at least one uniformly bounded Hilbert-space representation not similar to a unitary one.
records.statusQualification: Pisier and MO formulate the converse as an open question, and Monod's currently accessed primary problem page still calls it open. The latter is undated, not a2026publication or independent source lineage. One bounded root query plus declared worker discovery identified no relevant full-scope resolution; this does not certify the absence or reception of all possible claims. The namesake Weyl-algebra claim is a different target and remains unreviewed here. The displayed status is retained from the selected, previously reviewed input, with its bound qualifications; no fresh current-status certification is claimed here.
records.readerQuestion: Suppose every uniformly bounded linear action of a discrete group on a complex Hilbert space can be made length-preserving by a bounded invertible change of coordinates. Must the group admit a translation-invariant average on all bounded functions—that is, be amenable?
records.familyLabel: Dixmier unitarisability problem for discrete groups
records.whyItMatters: A proof would connect this universal representation property to invariant averaging on the group, without countability restrictions. A counterexample would separate the similarity-to-unitary property from amenability.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Characterize amenability of discrete groups by the similarity behavior of all uniformly bounded complex-Hilbert-space representations. No algorithmic, sharp quantitative or external-application guarantee is added.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Separate unitarisability from amenability by establishing a nonamenable group with the full universal similarity property. An existence proof suffices; no requirement of an explicit formula or construction is imposed.

records.canonicalTitle: NP-Hardness of Constant-Factor Approximation for Densest k-Subgraph
records.exactTarget: Let OPT(G,k)=max_{S subseteq V(G), |S|=k}|E(G[S])| for a finite simple undirected input graph G. Prove or refute the assertion that there exists an absolute constant epsilon>0 for which the promise problem of distinguishing OPT(G,k)>=t from OPT(G,k)<t/(1+epsilon), with input integers 1<=k<=|V(G)| and t>=1, is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time gap reductions. The target is any fixed nontrivial constant approximation gap for exactly k vertices, based on NP-hardness rather than a stronger average-case or exponential-time assumption.
records.statusQualification: The 25 May 2026 primary introduction states that even a 1.001 approximation NP-hardness result for DkS is unknown. Bounded searches including 2023–2026 and July/August/September 2026 found no later resolution; stronger-assumption and restricted-algorithm bounds are not ordinary NP-hardness.
records.readerQuestion: In a given graph, choose exactly k vertices to capture as many edges as possible. Is there a fixed approximation factor greater than one for which this task is NP-hard under deterministic polynomial-time reductions?
records.familyLabel: NP-Hardness of Constant-Factor Approximation for Densest k-Subgraph
records.whyItMatters: A proof would establish constant-gap hardness for selecting exactly k vertices, with no stronger complexity assumption in the reduction. It would rule out polynomial-time solutions to this promise problem unless P equals NP.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A deterministic polynomial-time reduction establishes ordinary NP-hardness for a fixed approximation gap; assuming P!=NP, the corresponding polynomial-time approximation guarantee is impossible.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A proof of the literal negation rules out every such fixed-gap NP-hardness assertion under the stated reductions. It does not on its own construct an approximation scheme.

records.canonicalTitle: Ivrii conjecture on periodic billiard orbits
records.exactTarget: For every integer n>=2 and every bounded connected open domain Ω in Euclidean R^n with C∞ boundary, prove the following assertion; neither convexity nor simple connectivity is assumed. Let M=B*∂Ω={(x,η) in T*∂Ω: |η|<1}, with the norm induced by the Euclidean metric and canonical symplectic (Liouville) volume μ=|ω^(n-1)|/(n-1)!, where ω is the canonical symplectic form. The billiard map β lifts (x,η) to the inward-pointing unit covector, follows the straight segment to its first subsequent boundary collision, and applies specular reflection, recording the tangential covector at that collision. Let M_reg be the set on which every forward and backward iterate is well-defined and nongrazing. For P=union over integers k>=2 of {z in M_reg: β^k(z)=z}, prove μ(P)=0. The integer k need not be the least period. Grazing collisions and any undefined singular continuation are excluded from M_reg; no rule continuing through them is imposed.

records.readerQuestion: For billiards in any bounded smooth connected region of dimension at least two, do exactly periodic, nongrazing paths occupy zero measure among starting boundary positions and directions? Only trajectories whose reflections remain well-defined in both time directions are counted.
records.familyLabel: Ivrii conjecture on periodic billiard orbits
records.whyItMatters: A proof would supply the dynamical hypothesis in Ivrii’s two-term asymptotic formula for Laplacian eigenvalue counts. A positive-measure periodic set would refute that hypothesis without itself disproving the spectral formula.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Establish the universal smooth Euclidean nonperiodicity condition and thereby supply the dynamical hypothesis in Ivrii's two-term Weyl asymptotics for the corresponding Laplacian problem. No numerical eigenvalue algorithm or claim for every billiard-like system is appended.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Establish an admissible ordinary smooth Euclidean billiard with positive-measure regular periodic points. This refutes the universal dynamical assertion; it need not produce an open periodic family or by itself refute the spectral asymptotic conclusion, whose measure-zero hypothesis is sufficient rather than asserted necessary.

records.canonicalTitle: Toms–Winter: Strict Comparison Implies Z-Stability
records.exactTarget: For every separable, simple, nuclear, non-elementary C*-algebra A, unital or nonunital, assert that strict comparison of positive elements implies A is isomorphic to A tensor_min Z, where Z is the Jiang–Su algebra. Non-elementary excludes algebras of compact operators. In the Cuntz semigroup Cu(A) of positive elements of A tensor K modulo Cuntz equivalence, strict comparison means: x≤y whenever phi(x)≤phi(y) for every ordered-semigroup functional phi:Cu(A)→[0,infinity] preserving zero and increasing sequential suprema, with strict inequality for every such phi for which 0<phi(y)<infinity. This is the convention following Conjecture 5.1 of Castillejos–Evington–Tikuisis–White. No UCT, unitality, finite trace-boundary, uniform Gamma or finite nuclear dimension hypothesis is added.
records.statusQualification: The May 8, 2026 version explicitly states Problem XVIII as the remaining open implication for precisely this non-elementary class. records.readerQuestion: In a separable simple nuclear C*-algebra that is not an algebra of compact operators, does strict comparison of positive elements force tensoring with the Jiang–Su algebra to leave it unchanged up to isomorphism? records.familyLabel: Toms–Winter: Strict Comparison Implies Z-Stability
records.whyItMatters: A proof would connect an order property of positive elements to this tensorial structural regularity. A counterexample would separate strict comparison from Jiang–Su absorption within the same class.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof completes the remaining regularity implication connecting strict comparison with Jiang–Su absorption in the full selected simple nuclear class, strengthening the structural basis of the classification program.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample separates comparison regularity from Jiang–Su absorption within the same class and requires revising the proposed regularity equivalence, without undoing established subclass classification theorems.

records.canonicalTitle: Brauer-Manin obstruction to the Hasse principle for K3 surfaces

records.canonicalTitle: Pugh–Shub Stable Ergodicity (C^r Density in Partial Hyperbolicity)
records.exactTarget: For every compact connected boundaryless smooth manifold M with a smooth probability volume m, and every r in [2,infinity] (including the C^infinity topology), is the following true? In the space PH_m^r(M) of volume-preserving C^r partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, maps that are C^1-stably ergodic among C^2 volume-preserving diffeomorphisms are C^r-dense. Thus every f in PH_m^r(M) and every relative C^r neighborhood U of f contain g such that some C^1 neighborhood V of g has every C^2 volume-preserving h in V ergodic for m. Use the usual C^r topology, with the Holder convention for nonintegral finite r. Partial hyperbolicity means a continuous Df-invariant dominated splitting TM=E^u+E^c+E^s: E^u and E^s are nontrivial, E^c may be zero, and for some common integer N>=1 the unstable unit vectors expand by >2, stable unit vectors contract by <1/2, and earlier nonzero bundles dominate later ones by a factor >2 under Df^N, pointwise at the same base point in that order. This is the ACW stability convention with the r>=2 range documented by RHRHU, not density among all conservative diffeomorphisms or only C^1-density.
records.statusQualification: The selected finer C^r-density assertion is classified open in this bounded review. ACW proves C^1-density; RHRHU proves the one-dimensional-center case. records.whyItMatters: The answer would determine whether the transition boundary between bounded and unbounded critical orbits carries positive planar area. A zero-area result would place that boundary in a planar null set.

records.canonicalTitle: Boundedness of Compact Hyperkahler Manifolds: Finiteness of Deformation Types in Each Dimension
records.exactTarget: For each integer n>=1, are there only finitely many deformation-equivalence classes of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic complex manifolds of complex dimension 2n? Such a manifold is smooth, simply connected and compact Kähler, with H^0(X,Omega_X^2) spanned by a holomorphic two-form nondegenerate everywhere. Deformation equivalence is the equivalence generated by occurrence as fibers in smooth proper holomorphic families of such manifolds over connected bases. No projectivity, polarization, lattice, second-Betti-number or fibration restriction is imposed. Resolve by proving finiteness in every fixed dimension or showing infinitely many deformation classes in one fixed dimension.
records.statusQualification: The unrestricted finiteness question remains open in the reviewed sources; the 2025 Engel–Filipazzi–Greer–Mauri–Svaldi theorem concerns Lagrangian-fibered varieties, and its extension to second Betti number at least five is conditional.
records.readerQuestion: In each fixed even complex dimension, are there only finitely many deformation types of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds? Deformations may pass through connected smooth proper holomorphic families; no projectivity, polarization or fibration assumption is imposed.
records.familyLabel: Hyperkähler fibrations and deformation types
records.whyItMatters: Finiteness would place a basic limit on the variety of these manifolds in any one dimension. It would establish that only finitely many deformation classes occur, without requiring an explicit classification of all of them.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: A proof would limit the number of deformation types of compact irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds in every fixed dimension, without itself classifying or explicitly constructing every type.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A disproof would establish infinitely many deformation types in one dimension and show that the known dimension-indexed families do not exhaust a finite list there.

records.readerQuestion: On the square lattice, assign independent edge-crossing times with a common nonnegative Borel probability law. Assume zero-time edges have probability below the square lattice's percolation threshold and the minimum of four independent times has finite second moment. Exactly which compact convex sets arise as deterministic large-scale growth shapes as this law varies?
records.familyLabel: Realizable Limit Shapes in Two-Dimensional First-Passage Percolation
records.whyItMatters: A necessary-and-sufficient characterization would identify the large-scale growth geometries obtainable from independent, identically distributed passage times under these assumptions. It would distinguish realizable shapes from those the model cannot produce.

records.readerQuestion: For square matrices over the integer group ring of any discrete group, is their determinant-like logarithmic spectral average always nonnegative? The average comes from the matrix's adjoint times itself, is normalized by matrix size, and omits the zero part of the spectrum.

records.whyItMatters: A proof would impose a universal lower bound on this logarithmic spectral quantity, even when the operator has a kernel. Failure would include either a negative value or divergence to minus infinity.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: The universal bound would ensure the determinant-class condition for integral group-ring matrices.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A counterexample would identify a discrete group outside the determinant-at-least-one class; by the known sofic case it would be nonsofic.

records.canonicalTitle: Hilbert's Tenth Problem over C(t) with named t
records.exactTarget: Let t be a fixed transcendental indeterminate and C(t) the field of complex rational functions. Determine whether there exists an algorithm (Turing machine) which, given any n >= 1 and any polynomial f in Z[t][x_1,...,x_n], presented by its finite list of integer coefficients and monomial exponents in t and the x_i, halts and correctly decides whether f = 0 has a solution (x_1,...,x_n) in C(t)^n. Equivalently, determine whether the existential (positive existential) theory of the structure (C(t); 0, 1, +, -, *, t), with a constant symbol naming t and no constants for other complex numbers, is decidable. Inputs with arbitrary complex coefficients, and the ring language without a symbol for t, are not part of this target.

records.readerQuestion: Can an algorithm always decide whether a polynomial equation has solutions that are complex rational functions of one formal variable t? The input coefficients are integer-coefficient polynomials in that same named t, and any finite number of unknowns is allowed.

records.whyItMatters: The answer would locate the decision boundary for these finitely encoded equations with the indeterminate t named. An algorithm must halt on every input; undecidability would rule out such a universal procedure for this exact coefficient language.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: Undecidability establishes an intrinsic limit to a total Turing procedure for this precisely encoded rational-function solvability problem. It does not imply that every individual equation or useful restricted family is intractable, settle the rational-number case, or automatically classify all curve function fields.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: Decidability gives a terminating correct test of existence for every specified input, contrasting with the at-least-two-complex-variable cases. records.canonicalTitle: Erdős Matching Conjecture
records.exactTarget: For all positive integers k,s,n with n>=ks, let F be a family of distinct k-element subsets of [n]={1,...,n} containing no s pairwise disjoint members. The conjecture asserts |F|<=max{binom(ks-1,k), binom(n,k)-binom(n-s+1,k)}. Here binom(a,k)=0 for integers 0<=a<k. For s=1 the family is empty, and k=1 is included as a trivial case. The two terms are attained by all k-subsets of a fixed (ks-1)-set and by all k-subsets meeting a fixed (s-1)-set, respectively. Their role is sharpness of the bound, not an additional classification of all equality families.

records.readerQuestion: When Schubert polynomials are multiplied, can each ordinary type-A coefficient be expressed as the number of combinatorial objects passing one uniform, efficient check? Each object must have polynomial-size encoding and be checkable in polynomial time from the three input permutations.
records.familyLabel: Positive Counting Rule for Type-A Schubert Structure Constants
records.whyItMatters: A proof would place these multiplication coefficients in #P through a single counting predicate. It would express their values as counts of efficiently verifiable finite objects for every encoded input triple.

resolutionConsequences.positiveBranch: The type-A coefficients would count uniformly polynomially checkable certificates without cancellation; this does not imply deterministic polynomial-time exact evaluation.
resolutionConsequences.negativeBranch: A nonexistence theorem would rule out this formalized uniform counting interpretation, not the known geometric nonnegativity of the coefficients.
